s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic photosensitive eruption with systemic and cutaneous manifestations
salient_findings: Photosensitive eruption involving face, neck, trunk, and extremities
Diffuse poikiloderma on upper chest, anterolateral thighs, and extensor arms
Erythematous, flat-topped papules on extensor joints of hands
key_facts: Previous treatments tried: systemic steroids, hydroxychloroquine, methotrexate, mycophenolate mofetil, cyclosporine, tacrolimus, tofacitinib, rituximab, and IVIG
Violaceous erythema on forehead and midface
Nailfold examination showed dilated capillary loops, capillary dropout, and ragged cuticles
Elevated serum IFN-β levels (8 pg/mL, normal ≤2 pg/mL)

differentials: Langerhans cell histiocytosis with skin involvement
per_call: Langerhans cell histiocytosis with skin involvement

shortlist.label: Juvenile dermatomyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of photosensitive eruption, violaceous erythema, poikiloderma, and nailfold changes, along with elevated serum IFN-β levels and presence of anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies, are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Lupus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Systemic and cutaneous manifestations, including photosensitivity, are common in lupus, and the presence of anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies supports this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Dermatomyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by skin manifestations, including photosensitive eruption and poikiloderma, and systemic involvement, such as myositis, which is supported by radiographic evidence

shortlist.label: Mixed connective tissue disease
shortlist.why_kept: Overlapping features of lupus, dermatomyositis, and other autoimmune diseases, along with the presence of anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies, make this a plausible diagnosis

shortlist.label: Sjögren's syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely, the presence of photosensitive eruption and systemic manifestations, such as myositis, could be consistent with Sjögren's syndrome, particularly if there are underlying autoimmune features

raw.rationale: The patient's age of onset, duration of symptoms, and clinical findings such as violaceous erythema, poikiloderma, and nailfold changes are consistent with juvenile dermatomyositis. The presence of elevated serum IFN-β levels and anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies, as well as radiographic evidence of myositis, further support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Lupus erythematosus
rejected.why: While lupus can present with similar skin and musculoskeletal symptoms, the patient's specific clinical findings and laboratory results are more consistent with juvenile dermatomyositis.

rejected.label: Dermatomyositis
rejected.why: Dermatomyositis typically presents in adults, and the patient's age of onset and duration of symptoms are more consistent with the juvenile form of the disease.

rejected.label: Mixed connective tissue disease
rejected.why: The patient's clinical findings and laboratory results do not demonstrate the characteristic overlap of lupus, scleroderma, and rheumatoid arthritis seen in mixed connective tissue disease.

rejected.label: Sjögren's syndrome
rejected.why: Sjögren's syndrome primarily presents with sicca symptoms and does not typically involve the skin and musculoskeletal findings seen in this patient.
